deep.reconstruction:
This page has no mathematics. It is a page of German history notes in Kurrent script, probably lecture notes or an excerpt, on the period of the Judges in ancient Israel. It continues the previous page's section 'Periode der jüdischen Republik nach Josua, von 1500–1000' and leads into the next page's 'Dritte Periode' (the monarchy).

Content, in order:
(1) The Israelite tribal confederation would have fallen apart had external misfortunes not pressed on it. The Philistines often harassed the Jews, with changing fortunes.
(2) Inspired men repeatedly rose to lead the nation and drive out its enemies. These were called 'Richter' (Judges). Othniel, Deborah and Samson are named as the best known.
(3) Already in this period Abimelech attempted to seize sole rule (Judges 9).
(4) The worship of Jehovah declined. Near the end of the period Samuel arose and restored it (c. 1150 BC). He was the last Judge and governed so prudently that he had the nation's general approval.
(5) In this favourable light he tried to make the office of judge hereditary in his family (cf. 1 Sam 8:1–3, his sons as judges).
(6) Because of constant wars the people felt the need for a military leader and demanded a king. Samuel designated Saul, 'the most handsome man in Israel' (cf. 1 Sam 9:2).

The page has no derivations, formulas or computations. The only numerical content is chronology: c. 1150 for Samuel, set within the stated span 1500–1000. The next page gives 1095–975 for three kings of 40 years each. The handwriting and subject suggest school or lecture notes, perhaps not in Gauss's own hand, despite the bundle label 'HB.Lagrange1816'.
errors: Not mathematical, so there are no mathematical errors to check.

Chronology: Samuel 'c. 1150' is earlier than the usual modern or traditional placement (roughly mid-11th century BC). It is consistent with early-19th-century textbook chronologies and with the notes' own scheme (Saul from 1095/1100).
The overall span 1500–1000 for the period of the Judges overlaps the next page's 'Monarchie von 1100'. This is an internal inconsistency in the notes' round-number periodization.

results.what: Narrative summary of the period of the Judges (Philistine oppression, Judges Othniel/Deborah/Samson, Abimelech's usurpation, Samuel's restoration of worship, the demand for a king, Saul's election)
results.modern_name: Biblical/ancient Israelite history (Book of Judges, 1 Samuel)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is routine historical/biblical narrative with no mathematical content. Nothing here would interest a historian of mathematics beyond its presence in the bundle, and it may not even be in Gauss's hand.

checkable.asserts: Context from the next page: three kings (Saul, David, Solomon) reigning 40 years each fill the stated span 1095–975 of the undivided kingdom.
The stated duration of the 'republic after Joshua' period is 500 years.

transcription_corrections: Folio number at top right reads '19', not '79'.

'Der Dienst des Jehovah hatte[?] längst fast gegen[?] hatte[?] dieser {+Periode+}[?]' should read approximately 'Der Dienst des Jehovah sank; fast gegen Ende dieser Periode stand Samuel auf'. The verb is uncertain ('sank'/'hing'), but 'gegen Ende dieser Periode' is clear.
'Sein Richteramt verwaltete er mit so vieler Klugheit' is confirmed.
Final word on the last line is 'Israel' (written on its own line).
